## Comprehensive Agent State Model & Dashboard Architecture Report

### 1. **Agent State Model** (hooks/use-websocket.ts)

#### `AgentClientState` Interface (lines 82-99)
Each agent in the browser has this client-side state:

```typescript
export interface AgentClientState {
  status: AgentStatus;              // Lifecycle state: idle | spawning | connected | thinking | done | disconnected | error
  messages: ChatMessage[];          // Processed chat messages for UI display
  rawMessages: ClaudeMessage[];     // Raw Claude NDJSON protocol messages (for debug view)
  label: string;                    // Agent display name (user-editable)
  tmuxSession: string | null;       // Associated tmux session ID
  createdAt: number;                // Unix timestamp of agent creation
  model?: string;                   // Model name (from system/init or spawn request)
  pinned?: boolean;                 // Whether pinned to top of sidebar
  iceboxed?: boolean;               // Whether archived/parked in icebox
  workspaceId?: string | null;      // Workspace assignment
}
```

#### **Agent Status Lifecycle** (lib/types.ts, lines 417-426)
```typescript
type AgentStatus = 
  | "idle"          // No process running, ready to spawn
  | "spawning"      // Process launched, waiting for CLI to connect
  | "connected"     // CLI connected and system/init received
  | "thinking"      // Waiting for assistant response
  | "done"          // Result message received, process finished
  | "disconnected"  // CLI unexpectedly disconnected
  | "error"         // Process crashed or unexpected failure
```

#### **Status Dot Coloring** (agent-sidebar.tsx, lines 24-33)
- `idle` → muted grey
- `spawning` → yellow with pulse
- `connected` → solid green
- `thinking` → blue with pulse
- `done` → muted grey
- `disconnected` → orange with pulse
- `error` → solid red

---

### 2. **Agent Data Flow Through the System**

#### **Initial Load Sequence** (use-websocket.ts, lines 11-18)
1. Browser connects to `ws://localhost:9900/browser`
2. Server sends `agent_list` (sidebar metadata only, NOT message histories)
3. Server sends `task_list` (all tasks)
4. `initialLoadDone` flag becomes true → sidebar loads
5. First agent is auto-selected if nothing was previously selected

#### **Lazy History Loading** (use-websocket.ts, lines 19-28)
- When user clicks an agent with `activeAgentId`, hook sends `{ type: "request_history", agentId }`
- Server responds with `message_history` containing all messages for that agent
- `loadedAgents` Set tracks which agents have been fetched (for instant switching back)
- `historyLoading` flag controls the "Loading messages..." spinner

#### **Live Message Relay** (use-websocket.ts, lines 630-699)
- CLI sends raw Claude NDJSON messages
- Server relays as `{ type: "relay", agentId, message: ClaudeMessage }`
- Browser converts via `relayChatMessage()` function into displayable `ChatMessage` objects
- Sound effects and notifications fire on: tool calls, done, error, control requests

#### **Message Deduplication** (use-websocket.ts, lines 311-313, server/ws.ts, lines 395-414)
- CLI sends **cumulative snapshots** for messages (each NDJSON line is complete state)
- Server deduplicates by message ID:
  - `assistant` messages → dedup by `message.id`
  - `user` messages → dedup by `uuid`
  - `system/init` → dedup by `init:<session_id>`
  - `result` → dedup by `result:<session_id>`
- Only the final snapshot is stored, reducing file size from 38MB → ~1MB for typical sessions

---

### 3. **Agent Properties Deep Dive**

#### **Core Identity**
- `agentId` — short random hex (e.g., `a1b2c3d4`)
- `label` — user-set display name, defaults to "new agent"
- `createdAt` — Unix milliseconds

#### **Execution Context**
- `tmuxSession` — tmux session name (format: `thos-agent-<id>`)
- `model` — Claude model (captured from `system/init` or spawn request)
- `sessionId` — Claude API session ID (set during `system/init`)

#### **Organization**
- `workspaceId` — links agent to a workspace directory
- `pinned` — boolean, shows in "pinned" section above active agents
- `iceboxed` — boolean, dims and moves to "icebox" section (parked for later)

#### **Workspace Scoping** (server/ws.ts, lines 344-360)
- Agents are filtered server-side by workspace scope per browser connection
- Sidebar shows agents only in the active workspace
- Tasks are also workspace-scoped

---

### 4. **Message Type Architecture** (lib/types.ts)

#### **ChatMessage** (displayable in UI, lines 459-486)
```typescript
export interface ChatMessage {
  id: string;                    // Unique message ID (generated client-side)
  role: "user" | "assistant" | "system";
  content: string;               // Rendered text
  timestamp: number;             // Client-side timestamp
  controlRequest?: {             // Present if tool approval needed
    id: string;
    tool_name: string;
    input: Record<string, unknown>;
    resolved?: boolean;
    allowed?: boolean;
  };
  userQuestion?: {               // Present if AskUserQuestion request
    requestId: string;
    questions: UserQuestion[];
    resolved?: boolean;
  };
  toolCalls?: ToolCallInfo[];    // Tool invocations extracted from assistant message

}
```

#### **ClaudeMessage** (raw NDJSON protocol, lines 108-115)
- `ClaudeSystemInit` — session metadata (model, cwd, tools available)
- `ClaudeAssistant` — assistant turn with content blocks
- `ClaudeResult` — terminal message with cost/duration
- `ClaudeControlRequest` — tool approval request
- `ClaudeSystemHook` — hook lifecycle events

- Results generate: `"Done — N turns, $X.XXXX, Ys"`

- Control requests get special UI treatment

├──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Workspace        │ StatusBar (connection, status, model, etc.)  │
│ Switcher         ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                  │ AgentSummary (raw NDJSON from system/init)   │
│ "agents"         ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Pinned (if any)  │ Message List (Virtuoso, condensed groups)    │
│ Active           │ - Messages                                   │
│ Icebox (if any)  │ - ControlRequest cards                       │
│ Archived (if any)│ - UserQuestion cards                         │
│                  │ - CondensedToolGroups (multiple tools)       │
│ [+] New agent    │                                              │

└──────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Diffs Panel** — File changes from Edit/Write tools, right side
- **Folder Browser** — Workspace creation/navigation modal

1. **Pinned** — `pinned=true && !iceboxed`
2. **Active** — `!pinned && !iceboxed && !ARCHIVED.has(status)`
3. **Icebox** — `iceboxed=true`
4. **Archived** — `!pinned && !iceboxed && ARCHIVED.has(status)`

Each section sorts by recency (most recent first).

---

### 6. **Key Components & Their Roles**

#### **AgentSidebar** (agent-sidebar.tsx)
- Renders 4 agent sections with status dots and labels
- Context menu (right-click): Pin/Icebox/Move/Rename/Kill/Clear/Delete
- Workspace switcher at top
- Loading skeleton during initial load
- Agent rows show: status dot, label, agent ID, workspace name, menu button

#### **Chat** (chat.tsx)
- Main message display using Virtuoso (virtual scrolling)
- Status bar with connection, agent status, model selector, toggle buttons
- Slash command menu (`/clear`, `/context`, etc.)
- Input form: Spawn (when idle/done) or Send (when connected/thinking)
- Loading spinner or "No agent selected" placeholder
- "Latest" scroll-to-bottom button

#### **StatusBar** (status-bar.tsx)
- Green/red connection dot
- Status label (idle/spawning/connected/thinking/done/disconnected/error)
- Agent label + model name
- Model dropdown (Sonnet 4, Opus 4, Qwen3, Devstral, or custom)
- Toggle buttons: Raw JSON view, Tasks, Diffs, Sidebar
- Notifications bell with inbox

#### **Message** (message.tsx)
- User messages: right-aligned, primary background
- Assistant messages: left-aligned, markdown-rendered
- System messages: centered, italic, muted
- Copy button on hover
- Relative timestamps with absolute time on hover
- DiffViewer inline for file-modifying tool calls

#### **ControlRequest** (control-request.tsx)
- Card showing tool approval request
- Allow/Deny buttons
- Tool name, input object, description

#### **UserQuestion** (user-question.tsx)
- Special UI for AskUserQuestion control requests
- Renders question text, radio/checkbox options, submit button

#### **CondensedToolGroup** (condensed-tool-group.tsx)
- Groups consecutive tool calls and their results
- Renders multi-tool messages more compactly
- DiffViewer integrated for file changes

#### **ContextUsageCard** (context-usage-card.tsx)
- Shows token usage from raw messages
- Displayed at bottom of chat when `/context` toggle is on

#### **TaskPanel / KanbanBoard** (kanban-board.tsx, task-*.tsx)
- Kanban board view with Todo/In-Progress/Done columns (+ Icebox)
- Task cards show title, description, priority badge
- Create, edit, delete, delegate to agent
- Workspace-scoped

#### **DiffsPanel** (diffs-panel.tsx)
- Shows all file changes (Edit/Write/MultiEdit) in current session
- DiffViewer rendering with syntax highlighting
- File path, before/after diffs

#### **FolderBrowser** (folder-browser.tsx)
- Directory listing modal for creating/selecting workspace paths
- Browse directories, create new workspace

#### **WorkspaceSwitcher** (workspace-switcher.tsx)
- Dropdown for active workspace selection
- Create, rename, delete workspaces
- "No workspace" option

---

### 7. **Server-Side Agent State** (server/ws.ts, lines 104-128)

The server maintains a richer `AgentState` for each agent:

```typescript
interface AgentState {
  agentId: string;
  claudeSocket: WebSocket | null;           // Current CLI connection
  tmuxSession: string | null;
  pendingPrompt: string | null;             // Queued until CLI connects
  status: AgentStatus;
  label: string;
  createdAt: number;
  sessionId: string | null;                 // Claude API session ID
  workspaceId: string | null;
  model: string | null;
  pinned: boolean;
  iceboxed: boolean;
  pendingControlRequests: Map<string, Record<string, unknown>>;  // For tool approvals
  messageHistory: ServerMessage[];          // Source of truth
  pendingMessages: string[];                // Queued while CLI disconnected
}
```

---

### 8. **Persistence Layer** (server/session-store.ts)

- **Per-agent files**: `.thos/sessions/<agentId>.json`
- **Contains**: agent metadata + compacted message history
- **Debounced save**: 150ms delay for streaming messages
- **Sync save**: Immediate for critical state (status changes)
- **Compaction**: History deduplicates cumulative snapshots on load
- **Restore logic**: On server restart, checks if tmux sessions are alive to determine `disconnected` vs `done`

---

### 9. **Critical Data Flow Examples**

#### **Spawning a New Agent**
1. User types prompt + selects model in chat input
2. Clicks "Spawn" → `spawnAgent(prompt, model)` 
3. Browser sends `{ type: "spawn", prompt, model }`
4. Server creates agent entry, spawns `claude --sdk-url ws://localhost:9900/claude/<agentId>`
5. CLI connects `/claude/<agentId>`, server forwards queued prompt on hook_response
6. CLI sends `system/init` → server captures model, workspaceId inferred from browser scope
7. Server broadcasts `agent_list` → sidebar updates
8. Server auto-selects the new agent (hook does `setActiveAgentId(agentId)`)
9. Browser requests history, server sends `message_history`

#### **Handling Tool Approval**
1. CLI sends `control_request` with tool name + input
2. Server relays to browser as `ChatMessage` with `controlRequest` field
3. UI renders ControlRequest card with Allow/Deny buttons
4. User clicks Allow → browser sends `{ type: "control_response", agentId, request_id, allow: true }`
5. Server forwards to CLI WebSocket `/claude/<agentId>`
6. Browser updates message to mark `resolved: true, allowed: true`

#### **Workspace Scoping**
1. Browser sends `{ type: "set_workspace", workspaceId }`
2. Server stores workspace scope per browser socket
3. On `agent_list`, `task_list`, agent spawns → server filters by workspace scope
4. Each browser tab can have different scope independently

---

### 10. **Key Files Summary**

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `hooks/use-websocket.ts` | React hook managing all agent/task/workspace state, WS connection, message conversion |
| `lib/types.ts` | TypeScript definitions for Claude protocol, browser↔server messages, UI state |
| `app/dashboard/page.tsx` | Layout orchestration, state distribution via props |
| `components/dashboard/agent-sidebar.tsx` | Agent list UI, pinned/active/icebox/archived sections, context menu |
| `components/dashboard/chat.tsx` | Main chat interface, message display, input handling |
| `components/dashboard/status-bar.tsx` | Connection/status indicators, model selector, toggle buttons |
| `components/dashboard/message.tsx` | Individual message rendering (user/assistant/system) |
| `server/ws.ts` | WebSocket relay, agent lifecycle, message routing, persistence |
| `server/session-store.ts` | File-based JSON persistence, debouncing, history compaction |
| `server/task-store.ts` | Task persistence |
| `server/workspace-store.ts` | Workspace persistence |

---

This architecture provides:
- **Multi-agent support** with independent message histories
- **Lazy loading** for fast initial page load
- **Workspace scoping** for project organization
- **File persistence** surviving server restarts
- **Resilient CLI reconnection** via tmux survival
- **Real-time sync** across multiple browser tabs
- **Comprehensive state tracking** from spawn through completion

### 7. **Server-Side Agent State** (server/ws.ts, lines 104-128)

The server maintains a richer `AgentState` for each agent:

```typescript
interface AgentState {
  agentId: string;
  claudeSocket: WebSocket | null;           // Current CLI connection
  tmuxSession: string | null;
  pendingPrompt: string | null;             // Queued until CLI connects
  status: AgentStatus;
  label: string;
  createdAt: number;
  sessionId: string | null;                 // Claude API session ID
  workspaceId: string | null;
  model: string | null;
  pinned: boolean;
  iceboxed: boolean;
  pendingControlRequests: Map<string, Record<string, unknown>>;  // For tool approvals
  messageHistory: ServerMessage[];          // Source of truth
  pendingMessages: string[];                // Queued while CLI disconnected
}
```

---

### 8. **Persistence Layer** (server/session-store.ts)

- **Per-agent files**: `.thos/sessions/<agentId>.json`
- **Contains**: agent metadata + compacted message history
- **Debounced save**: 150ms delay for streaming messages
- **Sync save**: Immediate for critical state (status changes)
- **Compaction**: History deduplicates cumulative snapshots on load
- **Restore logic**: On server restart, checks if tmux sessions are alive to determine `disconnected` vs `done`

---

### 9. **Critical Data Flow Examples**

#### **Spawning a New Agent**
1. User types prompt + selects model in chat input
2. Clicks "Spawn" → `spawnAgent(prompt, model)` 
3. Browser sends `{ type: "spawn", prompt, model }`
4. Server creates agent entry, spawns `claude --sdk-url ws://localhost:9900/claude/<agentId>`
5. CLI connects `/claude/<agentId>`, server forwards queued prompt on hook_response
6. CLI sends `system/init` → server captures model, workspaceId inferred from browser scope
7. Server broadcasts `agent_list` → sidebar updates
8. Server auto-selects the new agent (hook does `setActiveAgentId(agentId)`)
9. Browser requests history, server sends `message_history`

#### **Handling Tool Approval**
1. CLI sends `control_request` with tool name + input
2. Server relays to browser as `ChatMessage` with `controlRequest` field
3. UI renders ControlRequest card with Allow/Deny buttons
4. User clicks Allow → browser sends `{ type: "control_response", agentId, request_id, allow: true }`
5. Server forwards to CLI WebSocket `/claude/<agentId>`
6. Browser updates message to mark `resolved: true, allowed: true`

#### **Workspace Scoping**
1. Browser sends `{ type: "set_workspace", workspaceId }`
2. Server stores workspace scope per browser socket
3. On `agent_list`, `task_list`, agent spawns → server filters by workspace scope
4. Each browser tab can have different scope independently

---

### 10. **Key Files Summary**

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `hooks/use-websocket.ts` | React hook managing all agent/task/workspace state, WS connection, message conversion |
| `lib/types.ts` | TypeScript definitions for Claude protocol, browser↔server messages, UI state |
| `app/dashboard/page.tsx` | Layout orchestration, state distribution via props |
| `components/dashboard/agent-sidebar.tsx` | Agent list UI, pinned/active/icebox/archived sections, context menu |
| `components/dashboard/chat.tsx` | Main chat interface, message display, input handling |
| `components/dashboard/status-bar.tsx` | Connection/status indicators, model selector, toggle buttons |
| `components/dashboard/message.tsx` | Individual message rendering (user/assistant/system) |
| `server/ws.ts` | WebSocket relay, agent lifecycle, message routing, persistence |
| `server/session-store.ts` | File-based JSON persistence, debouncing, history compaction |
| `server/task-store.ts` | Task persistence |
| `server/workspace-store.ts` | Workspace persistence |

---

This architecture provides:
- **Multi-agent support** with independent message histories
- **Lazy loading** for fast initial page load
- **Workspace scoping** for project organization
- **File persistence** surviving server restarts
- **Resilient CLI reconnection** via tmux survival
- **Real-time sync** across multiple browser tabs
- **Comprehensive state tracking** from spawn through completion

I need to design a "Cozy Isometric Agent World" view for the thos project — a full-page tab/view showing agents as cute little characters working in an isometric room, Animal Crossing style. This is a Next.js 16 + React 19 + Tailwind CSS 4 + shadcn/ui project.

## Current Architecture

The project is a web UI for Claude Code agents. Key details:

- **Dashboard**: app/dashboard/page.tsx - main layout with sidebar + chat
- **Agent states**: idle, spawning, connected, thinking, done, disconnected, error
- **Agent properties**: agentId, label, status, model, toolCalls (current tools being used), pinned, iceboxed, workspaceId, createdAt
- **State hook**: hooks/use-websocket.ts exposes AgentClientState map, messages, etc.
- **Components**: components/dashboard/ has agent-sidebar, chat, status-bar, etc.
- **Styling**: Tailwind 4, dark mode default, cn() utility, OKLch colors

## What I Want

A new full-page view (toggleable from dashboard) that shows:

1. **An isometric room/scene** rendered with CSS (no canvas/WebGL for simplicity)
   - Floor tiles in isometric perspective
   - Desks/workstations where agents sit
   - Maybe some ambient decorations (plants, bookshelves, coffee machine)

2. **Agent characters** as cute minimal figures (CSS/SVG, not pixel art assets)
   - Each agent is a little figure at a desk
   - Visual state based on agent status:
     - idle → sitting relaxed, maybe sipping coffee
     - spawning → walking to their desk
     - connected → sitting down, ready
     - thinking → typing animation, maybe with thought bubble "..."
     - done → stretching, leaning back
     - disconnected → desk is empty, chair spun
     - error → little red ! above head
   - Agent label shown as a floating name tag
   - Maybe a small status indicator (colored dot matching existing sidebar colors)

3. **Ambient details**
   - Subtle idle animations (plant swaying, screen glow)
   - When an agent uses a tool, brief visual feedback (sparkles, file icon floating up)
   - Token/cost counter somewhere as a "resource" display

4. **Interaction**
   - Click an agent to select them (switches activeAgentId, so going back to chat shows their conversation)
   - Hover shows a tooltip with agent details (model, current tool, time active)

- Pure CSS/SVG for the isometric scene (no heavy dependencies like Three.js or Pixi)
- Should work with the existing useWebSocket hook for state
- Needs to handle 1-10+ agents dynamically (desks appear/disappear)
- Dark mode aesthetic matching existing dashboard
- Keep it lightweight — this is fun flavor, not a core feature
- Use CSS transforms for isometric projection (rotateX(60deg) rotateZ(-45deg) or similar)

## Questions to Answer

1. What's the best file structure for this?
2. How should the isometric grid and room be structured in CSS?
3. How should agent characters be rendered (pure CSS divs? inline SVG? emoji?)
4. How should animations work for different states?
5. How to wire it into the existing routing/navigation?
6. What's the minimal set of components needed?

Please provide a detailed implementation plan with specific component structure, CSS approach, and integration points.

- **Name tag**: Floating label above character (`agent.label`)
- **Status dot**: Same color scheme as sidebar (`STATUS_DOT` map, extracted to shared constant)

### Character Animations by Status

| Status | Character Pose | Animation |
|---|---|---|
| `idle` | Leaning back in chair, coffee cup nearby | Gentle sway, steam from cup |
| `spawning` | Walking toward desk from room entrance | CSS translate walk cycle |
| `connected` | Sitting upright at desk | Subtle breathing/bob |
| `thinking` | Leaning forward, hands on keyboard | Typing animation (arms move), thought bubble `...` pulses above head |
| `done` | Arms stretched up, leaning back | Stretch animation, then settle |
| `disconnected` | Chair empty, character absent | Chair slightly rotated, monitor dim |
| `error` | Slumped at desk | Red `!` floats above, gentle shake |

All animations via CSS `@keyframes` in `globals.css`.

### Interaction

- **Click agent/desk** → calls `onSelect(agentId)` and switches back to chat view (or just selects, user manually switches)
- **Hover agent** → tooltip with: label, model, status, current tool (from last `toolCalls`), time since creation

### Resource Bar (top of world view)

A thin bar at the top showing aggregate stats:
- Total agents active / total
- Combined thinking time
- A "vibe" indicator (all good = sun icon, errors = storm cloud)

## Integration into Dashboard

**`app/dashboard/page.tsx`**:
- Add state: `const [viewMode, setViewMode] = useState<"chat" | "world">("chat")`
- Conditionally render `<Chat>` or `<AgentWorld>` based on `viewMode`
- Pass `agents`, `agentOrder`, `activeAgentId`, `onSelect` to `<AgentWorld>`

**`components/dashboard/status-bar.tsx`**:
- Add a globe/tree icon toggle button (Lucide `TreePine` or `Globe`) next to existing toggles
- New props: `showWorld?: boolean`, `onToggleWorld?: () => void`

**`app/globals.css`**:
- Add `@keyframes` for: `iso-typing`, `iso-sway`, `iso-walk`, `iso-stretch`, `iso-breathe`, `iso-shake`, `iso-steam`, `thought-pulse`

## Shared Constant Extraction

Move `STATUS_DOT` color map from `agent-sidebar.tsx` into `lib/types.ts` (or a new `lib/agent-utils.ts`) so both the sidebar and world view can reuse it.
